haiku-low.q1: After the deploy record is written, before new instances start, one job applies pending migrations once. The old release must still work on the migrated schema.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that still uses the column or table has been retired.
haiku-low.q3: All 4 new instances must start, pass 3 consecutive /healthz checks, and pass smoke tests within 10 minutes. Otherwise the abort procedure runs and the old colour keeps serving.
haiku-low.q4: A single call repoints the public listener from the old target group to the new one, at step 9, after gating and smoke tests pass.
haiku-low.q5: Any complete 5-minute window from T+5 to T+15 with 5xx rate above 1%. Rollback repoints the listener to the old colour and stops new instances. Migrations are not reversed.
haiku-low.q6: Until T+30 minutes, an engineer can run catalog-web-rollback. After the old colour shuts down, a problem is fixed by a normal deploy of the previous release.
haiku-low.q7: Earlier migrations stay applied and the failing one rolls back. Phase becomes migration_failed, no new instances start, the old colour serves, and the pipeline alerts and releases the lock.
haiku-low.q8: The pipeline reads the live colour from the load balancer listener each time. The other colour is idle. Old and new colours are recorded in state.json.
haiku-low.q9: A shared pipeline concurrency group acts as a lock. A run holds it from step 2 until step 14. Only the newest waiting run proceeds; others are superseded.
haiku-low.q10: Smoke tests run directly against the new instances' addresses, not through the load balancer, so users stay on the old colour.
haiku-low.q11: A single job in step 5 runs the migration tool. A database advisory lock stops concurrent runs, and the tool's tracking table records applied migrations.
haiku-low.q12: Their instances are stopped immediately, not kept for debugging. The idle colour then has 0 instances; the next deploy's step 3 stops any leftovers.

sonnet.q1: Step 5, after the deploy record is written and before the new colour's instances start (step 6). The old release must still work against the migrated schema (it keeps serving).
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that still uses the column or table has been retired.
sonnet.q3: All 4 new instances must be started and registered, pass the health gate (3 consecutive /healthz passes each), and pass the smoke tests, all within 10 minutes of instances_started_at. If not, the abort procedure runs: phase=aborted, new instances stopped, listener untouched, pipeline fails and alerts, lock released. A failed smoke test aborts immediately.
sonnet.q4: In one step (step 9): a single call repoints the public load balancer listener from the old target group to the new one. The pipeline reads it back to confirm, then sets phase=switched and switched_at (T).
sonnet.q5: Trigger: any 5xx-rate window (trailing 5 min, checked each minute from T+5 to T+15) above 1% (an engineer can also trigger a manual rollback via catalog-web-rollback). Rollback sets phase=rolling_back, repoints the listener to the old target group, confirms, sets rolled_back, stops the new colour's 4 instances, marks the deploy failed, alerts and releases the lock. It leaves migrations unreversed (schema stays migrated) and the release on main.
sonnet.q6: Until step 13 shuts the old colour down at T+30 minutes (rollback via catalog-web-rollback is allowed from T until then). After that, catalog-web-rollback refuses to run; a problem is handled by a normal deploy of the previous release (steps 2 to 14, with step 5 doing nothing).
sonnet.q7: The failing migration rolls back (its own transaction), but earlier migrations in the same run stay applied (harmless since additive). phase=migration_failed, no new instances are started, the old colour keeps serving, the pipeline alerts and releases the lock.
sonnet.q8: The live colour is read from the load balancer's public listener each time (never stored). It becomes old_colour and the other colour is new_colour (the one receiving the release). Both are then recorded in the deploy record, deploys/catalog-web/state.json in the pipeline's state bucket.
sonnet.q9: A shared pipeline concurrency group for all catalog-web deploy runs acts as the lock. A run holds it from step 2 until step 14 (close the deploy), or until the pipeline's own timeout releases it if step 14 fails. Queued merges wait; only the newest waiting run proceeds and the rest are superseded.
sonnet.q10: The smoke tests run directly against the new instances' addresses, not through the load balancer, so no user traffic is involved.
sonnet.q11: A single job in step 5 runs the release's pending migrations, via the migration tool. Each migration runs in its own transaction, the tool takes a database advisory lock so two runs cannot migrate at once, and applied migrations are tracked in a table in the database (so already-applied ones are not rerun; if nothing is pending it does nothing).
sonnet.q12: They are stopped immediately (abort: step 2 of the abort procedure; rollback: stopped after repointing), so the idle colour has 0 running instances. If any are left running after a failure, step 3 of the next deploy stops them (safe since the listener does not point at them).
